title: Recurring residential cleaning company (W-2 team model, biweekly plans)
product_service: Scheduled weekly/biweekly/monthly whole-home cleaning by 2-person W-2 teams, plus deep cleans and move-in/out cleans.
target_customer: Dual-income and affluent households (often $100k+ income) in Chicago suburbs and dense city neighborhoods.
purchase_motivation: Time savings, consistency, trust (bonded/insured vetted staff vs. independent cleaners).
spending_evidence: MaidPro 245 franchises averaged $430,998 gross consumer sales in 2025 (median $380,083; ~2,423 jobs/unit) [B, WS18-S004]; Molly Maid average $173.43 per cleaning and 91% of cleanings for recurring customers in 2024 [B, WS18-S002]; 432 Molly Maid US franchises open end-2025 [B, WS18-S003].
representative_operators: Molly Maid (Neighborly) — 432 US franchises, ~$173/clean average [B, WS18-S002/S003]
MaidPro — 245 reporting franchises, avg $431k sales [B, WS18-S004]
The Maids — large franchise system (Item 19 not retrieved)
Thousands of independent owner-operators and solo cleaners (not quantified)
revenue_mechanism: Price per visit (flat or hourly) × visits; recurring plans billed per visit to card on file.
typical_transaction_value: ~$150-$230 per recurring clean (Molly Maid avg $173.43, MaidPro ≈$178/job) [B]; recurring client ≈ $3,500-$5,000/yr at biweekly frequency [E].
direct_costs: Cleaner wages + payroll taxes + workers' comp (largest cost), drive time/mileage, supplies, damage claims.
contribution_profit_note: Assumed labor 45-55% of revenue for W-2 team model; contribution ≈$60-90 per $175 clean before marketing and office [E]. No franchisor cost data captured.
working_capital_note: Card charged at/after each visit; payroll biweekly — minimal receivables. Main cash need is payroll during ramp and marketing.
sales_cycle: Days: online quote → first clean within 1-2 weeks.
repeat_purchase: recurring — 91% of Molly Maid cleanings are for recurring customers [B, WS18-S002]
acquisition_channels: Direct mail to high-income zip codes
customer_accessibility: High — households search actively and switch easily; affluent zip codes identifiable from Census data.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed — supplies are commodity retail/wholesale; binding constraint is labor supply, not goods.
competitive_intensity: high — national franchises plus very large informal/independent cleaner supply undercutting on price.
entry_strategy: Reliability and vetted W-2 staff at mid-premium price; instant online quoting/booking; same team every visit; target suburbs where franchise territories are thin.
licenses: No Illinois state licence for house cleaning; house cleaning is not 'home repair and remodeling' [A, WS18-S010]. Needs entity registration, possibly municipal business licence (Chicago/suburb specifics MISSING), workers' comp (mandatory for employees in IL), general liability and janitorial bond.
regulatory_barriers: Low. Employment-law exposure (worker classification, Illinois paid leave, Chicago minimum wage) is the main regulatory risk.
operational_risks: Cleaner turnover and no-shows, theft/damage allegations, quality consistency, scheduling churn.
financial_risks: Payroll grows ahead of revenue; customer churn requires constant marketing; wage inflation.
geographic_constraints: Route density matters; serve a 15-20 mile radius per office.
founder_expertise: Hiring/training hourly workers, quality-control systems, local digital marketing.
staffing: Hire 2-4 cleaners in month 1-3; office/scheduling manager at ~$300-400k revenue; team leads per 3-4 teams.
automation_potential: Online instant quoting, routing/scheduling optimization, AI call/text intake, review management, applicant screening. Cleaning itself stays manual.
delegation_potential: Good — franchise systems run with owner-managers and office managers; standard hourly roles.
scalability: Moderate: multi-territory metro operator to ~$1-3M revenue (top MaidPro quartile averaged $925k [B, WS18-S004]); labor-limited.
expansion: Move-out/realtor cleans, Airbnb turnovers, post-construction cleaning, window cleaning add-on, adjacent suburbs.
roic_note: Capital at risk ~$20-50k including ramp losses; yr3 profit $40-140k → roughly 150-400% annual return on capital [E].
critical_assumptions: Labor cost ≤55% of revenue in Chicago market at ~$18-22/hr wages
Can recruit and retain reliable cleaners faster than demand grows
Customer acquisition cost recoverable within ~3 months of recurring service
unanswered_questions: Operating margin data for franchise or independent maid services (no Item 19 cost data captured)
Municipal business licence requirements in target suburbs and Chicago
failure_modes: Owner becomes the backup cleaner and scheduler; burnout
Underpricing to compete with informal cleaners leaves no margin
score_rationale: Cash/feasibility high (paid at service, no licence). Access 7: households search and switch easily. FCF 4: typical franchise unit ~$380-430k sales implies ~$50-100k profit; top operators higher. Entry 4: crowded, easily copied. Scale 4: labor-limited local ceiling.
preliminary_verdict: advance — reliable, low-capital cash generator with strong access and delegation; ceiling moderate unless multi-territory.

title: Non-medical in-home senior care agency (IDPH-licensed Home Services agency)
subindustry: Non-medical home care (companion, personal care, ADL assistance)
product_service: Hourly and live-in caregivers for older adults: bathing/dressing help, meals, housekeeping, companionship, dementia support; private pay, long-term-care insurance, VA, and Illinois Community Care Program (Medicaid waiver).
target_customer: Seniors 75+ and their adult children; referral sources: hospital discharge planners, senior living, elder-law attorneys, home health agencies.
purchase_motivation: Need-based: safety, avoiding or delaying assisted living/nursing home, family caregiver burnout, post-hospital recovery.
spending_evidence: Home Instead 603 US franchises averaged $2,609,616 gross sales in 2024 (median $2,261,503) and 78,428 client hours (~$33/hr) [B, WS18-S005]; Illinois CCP pays $30.80/hr for in-home service from 1/1/2026 [A, WS18-S020]; aide jobs projected +18% 2025-35 [C, WS18-S021].
representative_operators: Home Instead — 603 franchises, avg $2.6M (mature, median tenure 15+ yrs) [B, WS18-S005]
A Place At Home — 34 operational outlets incl. Illinois 19 (opened 2021) [B, WS18-S006]
Comfort Keepers, Right at Home, Visiting Angels, BrightStar (Item 19 not retrieved)
Addus HomeCare — large Illinois CCP provider (10-K not retrieved)
revenue_mechanism: Hourly bill rate × client hours (private pay typically higher than $30.80 CCP rate); minimum shift lengths; live-in day rates.
typical_transaction_value: ~$30-38/hour; typical client 15-40 hrs/week ≈ $25k-$75k/yr per client [E; Home Instead implied ~$33/hr B, WS18-S005].
direct_costs: Caregiver wages, payroll taxes, workers' comp, overtime, mileage, training.
contribution_profit_note: A Place At Home outlets report gross profit after direct labor of ~42-64% (most 45-55%) [B, WS18-S006]; office staff, recruiting, marketing and insurance consume much of this — assumed operating margin 8-15% at maturity [E].
working_capital_note: Caregivers paid weekly/biweekly; private pay can be billed weekly in advance or on card, but LTC insurance, VA and CCP pay in arrears (assumed 30-60 days) — meaningful payroll float as census grows.
sales_cycle: Days once a family is in crisis; months to build referral-source trust.
repeat_purchase: recurring — ongoing weekly hours until client transitions or dies; average client tenure MISSING.
acquisition_channels: Senior living and independent living communities
Elder-law attorneys, geriatric care managers, financial advisors
Illinois Community Care Program care coordination units
customer_accessibility: Moderate — families search urgently online, but referral sources take months of relationship-building and track record.
supplier_accessibility: Caregiver labor supply is the binding constraint; national shortage widely reported (not quantified here).
competitive_intensity: high — many franchised and independent agencies in Chicagoland; differentiation via caregiver quality and responsiveness.
entry_strategy: Specialize (dementia, hospital-to-home transitions, 24/7 live-in), guarantee fast start (<24h), pay caregivers above market with guaranteed hours; build dense referral network in 2-3 suburbs.
licenses: IDPH Home Services Agency licence required (210 ILCS 55; 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245); Manager Qualification Review; Health Care Worker Background Check Act fingerprinting [A, WS18-S013]. Fee, manager qualifications and worker training hours MISSING. CCP provider contracting with IL Dept on Aging is separate (process MISSING).
regulatory_barriers: Moderate: state licensure and surveys, background checks, wage-and-hour (federal home care overtime rule), Medicaid program compliance if CCP.
operational_risks: Caregiver recruiting/retention, missed shifts, client injury or abuse allegations, 24/7 on-call scheduling.
financial_risks: Wage inflation vs. bill rates; CCP rate fixed by state; payroll float; workers' comp and liability claims.
founder_expertise: Healthcare-adjacent operations, compliance, caregiver recruiting, referral-source sales. No clinical licence needed for non-medical services.
staffing: Qualified agency manager (if founder lacks qualification) and care coordinator from day 1; caregivers per client; scheduler/recruiter by ~$500k revenue.
automation_potential: Scheduling/matching, caregiver recruiting funnels, EVV/time capture, intake and family updates, billing. Care itself is human.
delegation_potential: Strong — commonly run by general managers; standard roles (care manager, scheduler, recruiter).
scalability: Good regional runway: Home Instead units mature to $2-3M+ revenue; multiple territories/branches possible; A Place At Home outlets reached ~$1.5M avg sales by months 37-48 [B, WS18-S006].
expansion: Home care + private-duty nursing (requires Home Nursing licence), senior move management, home modifications referrals, adult day, geriatric care management.
roic_note: Capital at risk ~$60-120k (licensing, insurance, office, 12-18 months of ramp losses, payroll float); yr3-5 profit $100-300k → ~100-250% [E].
critical_assumptions: Private-pay bill rate in Chicago suburbs ≥$34/hr while paying caregivers $18-21/hr
Founder or hired manager can satisfy IDPH manager qualifications
Ramp similar to A Place At Home young outlets (~$500k sales in year 2)
unanswered_questions: IDPH Home Services licence fee, manager qualification and training-hour requirements (77 IAC 245 not retrieved — ilga.gov 503)
Chicago-area private-pay rates and caregiver wages
Operating (not gross) margins of independent agencies
CCP provider contracting process and payment timing
failure_modes: Cannot staff hours sold — reputation collapse
Thin margin if dependent on CCP Medicaid rate
Founder underestimates 24/7 on-call burden and referral-sales time
score_rationale: Resilience 8: needs-based, demographic tailwind, public payer. FCF 6 and scale 6: mature units $2M+ sales, ramp evidence from young outlets. Access 6: referral trust takes time. Feasibility 6: state licence obtainable without professional credential but adds time. Cash 6: payroll float with arrears payers.
preliminary_verdict: advance — best combination of durable demand, delegation and ceiling in WS18; licensing and caregiver supply are the key diligence items.

title: Junk removal and hauling (with optional dumpster rental)
product_service: Full-service removal of household junk, furniture, appliances, estate and renovation debris by a 2-person truck crew; small roll-off/dumpster rentals.
target_customer: Homeowners and renters (moves, cleanouts, estates), realtors, property managers, small contractors.
purchase_motivation: Urgent, labor-saving disposal; moving, estate settlement, renovation.
spending_evidence: Junk King 166 US units averaged $553,959 gross sales in 2024 (median $435,663; bottom quartile $193,696), avg $399/job [B, WS18-S001].
representative_operators: Junk King — 172 US units, avg $554k [B, WS18-S001]
1-800-GOT-JUNK, College Hunks Hauling Junk, JunkLuggers (Item 19 not retrieved)
revenue_mechanism: Volume-based price per load fraction × jobs; dumpster rental per drop.
direct_costs: Crew labor (20.6% of sales), dump fees (7.2%), fuel (3.3%) per Junk King survey; franchise licence 8% and call-centre 5% avoided by independent [B, WS18-S001].
contribution_profit_note: Junk King franchise gross profit 56.3% after franchise fees, before rent, truck payments, insurance, marketing [B, WS18-S001]; independent ≈65-70% before self-funded marketing and call handling [E].
working_capital_note: Paid at job completion; dump fees same-day; truck purchase/lease is the main capital need.
repeat_purchase: occasional — repeat via realtors/property managers; consumers infrequent.
acquisition_channels: Estate attorneys and senior move managers
customer_accessibility: High — buyers search at moment of need.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed — trucks/trailers available used; transfer stations and recyclers accessible (fees vary by municipality).
competitive_intensity: high — three national franchise brands plus many independents.
entry_strategy: Same-day service, photo/video instant quotes, donation/recycling diversion story, B2B accounts with property managers and realtors.
licenses: No Illinois licence specific to junk removal identified. Whether ICC household goods licence applies to hauling customers' goods for disposal is unclear [A for licence existence, WS18-S014]. Municipal waste-hauler licensing (Chicago/suburbs) MISSING. Commercial auto insurance, GL, workers' comp.
regulatory_barriers: Low; disposal rules for appliances (refrigerant), electronics (Illinois electronics landfill ban — not verified), tires, paint.
operational_risks: Worker injury (lifting), truck downtime, property damage.
financial_risks: Truck capital; marketing costs; seasonality (winter slower).
founder_expertise: Pricing by volume, crew management, digital marketing.
staffing: Founder + 1 helper initially; crews of 2 per truck; dispatcher at 2-3 trucks.
automation_potential: Photo-based quoting, AI phone/text booking, routing. Labor remains manual.
delegation_potential: Good — crew leads and dispatcher are standard roles.
scalability: Moderate: add trucks within metro; top Junk King quartile ~$1.1M [B, WS18-S001].
expansion: Dumpster rental, estate cleanouts, demolition (light), donation pickup partnerships, hoarding cleanouts.
critical_assumptions: Independent can replace franchise call-centre/brand with own marketing at ≤10% of sales
Dump fees in Chicagoland similar to system average 7.2%
unanswered_questions: Customer acquisition cost per job in Chicago
failure_modes: Underpriced loads after dump fees and labor
score_rationale: Strong FDD cost data: ~56% GP for franchisees after 13% fees. Access 7 (urgent search), cash 9. Entry 4: crowded with national brands. FCF 4: median unit ~$436k sales implies ~$60-100k owner profit.
preliminary_verdict: hold — well-evidenced, delegable cash business but commoditized with a moderate ceiling.

title: Lawn fertilization & weed-control subscription route (IDOA-licensed)
product_service: 5-7 seasonal applications per year (fertilizer, pre-emergent, broadleaf weed control), plus aeration/overseeding, grub control; sold as an auto-renewing annual program.
target_customer: Suburban single-family homeowners with turf lawns.
purchase_motivation: Curb appeal, convenience, HOA norms; avoiding DIY chemical handling.
spending_evidence: Weed Man 149 US locations averaged $2,042,514 gross sales in 2025 (median $1,693,230; bottom quartile avg $347,272) [B, WS18-S007].
representative_operators: Weed Man USA — 153 locations, avg $2.04M [B, WS18-S007]
Lawn Doctor, Spring-Green (Illinois-based franchisor) — Item 19 not retrieved
revenue_mechanism: Per-application price scaled by lawn square footage × applications per season; prepay discounts.
typical_transaction_value: Assumed ~$50-90 per application, ~$350-600 per customer per year [E].
contribution_profit_note: Applications take ~15-30 minutes per lawn in dense routes; contribution assumed 45-60% before marketing/overhead [E]; no Item 19 cost data captured.
working_capital_note: Many customers prepay the season (discount) or autopay per application; product bought in spring before revenue.
sales_cycle: Seasonal selling window Feb-May; decision in days.
repeat_purchase: recurring — auto-renewing annual programs; churn rate MISSING.
customer_accessibility: Good — homeowners identifiable by parcel/lot data; quotes possible remotely from aerial imagery.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed (assumed) — product available from turf distributors; equipment standard.
competitive_intensity: high — TruGreen and franchises plus local operators; service quality complaints about large players create openings.
entry_strategy: Hyper-dense subdivision targeting, remote instant quoting, service guarantee, hybrid/organic program option, bundle with mosquito (WS18-006) and holiday lighting (WS18-027) for year-round revenue.
licenses: IDOA commercial applicator licence ($300/3 yrs) and commercial operator licences ($240) for technicians; exam required [A, WS18-S019]. Lawn Care Products Application and Notice Act obligations (posting/notification) not verified. Landscaping is excluded from the Home Repair Act [A, WS18-S010].
regulatory_barriers: Moderate: pesticide licensing and recordkeeping; possible local pesticide restrictions (MISSING).
operational_risks: Weather windows, chemical misapplication/drift claims, technician licensing turnover.
financial_risks: Seasonal cash (Apr-Nov); spring inventory; CAC high in year 1.
geographic_constraints: Route density within 10-15 miles of base; Chicago suburbs suit (large turf lots).
founder_expertise: Turf agronomy basics, pesticide licensing, route marketing.
staffing: Founder licensed applicator year 1; seasonal licensed operators by year 2; office/sales help in spring.
automation_potential: Aerial-measurement quoting, route optimization, CRM/renewals, AI phone intake. Application remains manual.
delegation_potential: Good — technicians and branch managers are standard roles in a mature franchise model.
scalability: Good: mature Weed Man units exceed $1.7M median; density compounding and multi-branch expansion possible.
expansion: Mosquito/tick, aeration/seeding, tree & shrub care, perimeter pest, holiday lighting, later acquisition of small routes.
roic_note: ~$40-80k at risk; yr3 profit $50-175k → ~100-250% [E]; route value accretes (sellable).
critical_assumptions: Route density allows 20+ applications per tech-day
Mature-system revenues (long tenure) are reachable gradually by new entrant
unanswered_questions: Weed Man/Lawn Doctor operating margins and young-unit revenue
Lawn Care Products Application and Notice Act requirements
failure_modes: Low density → drive time kills margin
Spring capacity crunch when hiring licensed techs
score_rationale: Recurring auto-renew route with B-level revenue evidence of large mature units; density builds a moat (entry 5). Feasibility 7: obtainable exam-based licence. Cash 9: prepay common.
preliminary_verdict: advance — recurring, density-driven route with documented mature-unit revenue; year-round bundling needed for Chicago seasonality.

title: Residential lawn mowing & snow removal maintenance route
product_service: Weekly mowing/trimming April-November and seasonal snow plowing/shoveling contracts December-March for homes and small HOAs.
target_customer: Suburban homeowners, seniors, small HOAs/townhome associations.
purchase_motivation: Time savings, physical inability (seniors), reliability during snow events.
spending_evidence: The Grounds Guys units open 3+ years averaged $820,392 (median $533,092); units <3 years averaged $392,054 (median $294,312) in 2025 [C, WS18-S023].
revenue_mechanism: Per-visit or monthly mowing price; seasonal snow contracts (flat) or per-push pricing.
typical_transaction_value: Assumed $40-70 per mow; $400-1,200 per snow season per driveway [E].
direct_costs: Crew labor, mowers/trucks/plows, fuel, salt, equipment repair.
contribution_profit_note: Labor-heavy; assumed owner net 8-15% of revenue [E].
working_capital_note: Monthly billing; snow events billed after storms; equipment upfront.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed — equipment dealers, salt suppliers (salt shortages occur in hard winters — not quantified).
competitive_intensity: extreme — very low barriers, many cash-pay operators.
entry_strategy: Reliability, density, bundled year-round plans for seniors.
licenses: No state licence for mowing; landscaping excluded from Home Repair Act [A, WS18-S010]; pesticide applications would need IDOA licence [A, WS18-S019].
regulatory_barriers: Low; H-2B seasonal labor rules if used.
operational_risks: Weather variance (snow), equipment breakdown, seasonal labor.
financial_risks: Low-snow winters crush per-push revenue; fixed equipment costs.
staffing: Crew of 2-3 per truck; seasonal hires.
automation_potential: Routing, billing, quoting via aerial imagery. Work is manual.
delegation_potential: Moderate — crew leaders available but seasonal turnover high.
critical_assumptions: Owner net margin ≤15% in a commodity labor service
unanswered_questions: Chicago snow contract pricing and variance
score_rationale: Easy entry and access but extreme competition and thin margins; better as an add-on to fertilization routes.
preliminary_verdict: hold — viable cash business but low margin; consider only bundled with WS18-004.

title: Mosquito & tick barrier-spray seasonal subscription
product_service: Barrier treatments of yard foliage every ~3 weeks May-September, auto-renewing season plans; event one-off sprays.
target_customer: Suburban homeowners with wooded/landscaped yards, families with children/pets.
purchase_motivation: Outdoor comfort, disease worry (West Nile, Lyme), events.
spending_evidence: MISSING — Mosquito Joe/Mosquito Squad Item 19 not retrieved (search budget exhausted).
revenue_mechanism: Per-treatment price × ~7-9 treatments/season, prepaid or autopay.
direct_costs: Insecticide, technician labor (15-30 min/yard), backpack mist blowers, truck/fuel.
contribution_profit_note: High product margin; labor-light per stop [E].
working_capital_note: Prepaid or autopay; product purchased in spring.
competitive_intensity: moderate — franchise brands plus lawn/pest operators.
entry_strategy: Bundle with fertilization route (shared licence, truck, customer base) for higher revenue per stop.
licenses: IDOA commercial applicator/operator licence; mosquito category training offered [A, WS18-S019]. Local restrictions MISSING.
regulatory_barriers: Moderate — pesticide use scrutiny (pollinator impacts); potential municipal limits.
financial_risks: Revenue concentrated in 5 months; winter idle costs.
scalability: Moderate; strongest as a line within a lawn/pest company.
expansion: Lawn fertilization, perimeter pest, tick tubes, holiday lighting off-season.
roic_note: Low capital ($15-40k at risk) vs $30-110k profit → ~150-300% [E].
critical_assumptions: Season pricing and retention similar to franchise systems
failure_modes: Short season can't cover annual fixed costs
score_rationale: High margin, low capital, recurring; seasonal and evidence weak (E).
preliminary_verdict: hold — attractive as an add-on line to WS18-004 rather than a standalone company.

title: Residential pest control quarterly service plans (IDPH-licensed)
product_service: Initial service plus quarterly perimeter/interior treatments for ants, spiders, cockroaches, rodents; one-off rodent exclusion, bed bug and wasp jobs.
target_customer: Single-family and 2-6 flat owners in Chicago and suburbs; small landlords.
purchase_motivation: Urgent infestations (mice/rats common in Chicago-area housing stock — not quantified), ongoing prevention.
spending_evidence: MISSING — Rollins/Rentokil-Terminix 10-K data not retrieved (EDGAR rate-limited); no Item 19 captured.
revenue_mechanism: Initial fee + quarterly recurring charge on autopay; one-off premium jobs.
working_capital_note: Autopay recurring; low inventory.
sales_cycle: Same day for infestations; days for plans.
customer_accessibility: Good — urgent search demand plus D2D.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed — distributors (e.g., Univar/Target Specialty) sell to licensed businesses.
entry_strategy: Rodent specialization for Chicago bungalows/2-flats, guaranteed response, landlord portfolio contracts, later wildlife (WS18-033) bundle.
licenses: IDPH Commercial Structural Pest Control Business licence (annual) requiring at least one Certified Technician who passes General Standards exam (70%), certificate of insurance on file [A, WS18-S018]. Fees MISSING.
regulatory_barriers: Moderate — exam-based certification obtainable in months; recordkeeping; restricted-use pesticide categories.
founder_expertise: Become certified technician; route sales; entomology basics.
staffing: Founder as certified tech year 1; add techs and a seasonal sales team.
automation_potential: Routing, AI intake, renewal billing, inspection photo logs.
delegation_potential: Good — standard technician and service manager roles.
scalability: Good — route density compounding; recurring revenue books are routinely bought by consolidators (deal data not retrieved).
expansion: Termite (inspection for real estate), wildlife, mosquito, commercial accounts (WS05 overlap).
critical_assumptions: Founder can pass certification within ~3 months
Quarterly pricing holds in Chicago market
unanswered_questions: IDPH licence fees and insurance minimums
score_rationale: Resilience 8: essential recurring service. Feasibility 6: certification needed but obtainable. Entry 4: crowded. Evidence E for economics.
preliminary_verdict: advance — durable recurring route with exam-based (not credential) licensing; needs economic evidence.

title: Handyman service company (W-2 craftsmen, small residential repairs)
product_service: Small repairs and installs (drywall, doors, fixtures, carpentry, TV mounting, caulking) billed per job by employed craftsmen.
target_customer: Homeowners 45+, seniors, landlords, realtors preparing listings.
purchase_motivation: Lack of time/skill; trades won't take small jobs.
spending_evidence: Mr. Handyman single-territory franchisees averaged $773,574 (median $580,422) in 2025; avg $742 per job [B, WS18-S008].
revenue_mechanism: Hourly labor + materials markup + service charge.
contribution_profit_note: Ace Handyman single territories: gross profit ~43-55% of revenue but owner discretionary income only 2-11% (top quartile $49,793 on $775k); multi-territory top quartile 15% ($223,597 on $1.51M) [B, WS18-S009]. Adding back ~8% royalty/brand fund → independent ~10-19% [E].
working_capital_note: Paid on completion (deposits for larger jobs); materials bought per job.
repeat_purchase: occasional — repeat customers with honey-do lists; maintenance memberships possible.
customer_accessibility: High — strong unmet demand for small jobs.
entry_strategy: Reliability and scheduling guarantee; targeted at seniors and realtors; maintenance membership.
licenses: Home Repair and Remodeling Act: written contract >$1,000, consumer-rights pamphlet, liability insurance ($100k/$300k bodily injury, $50k property, $10k improper repairs as enacted) [A, WS18-S010, WS18-S011]. Chicago/municipal contractor licensing and permits for regulated work (electrical/plumbing licences) MISSING — must avoid licensed trades.
regulatory_barriers: Moderate — scope creep into licensed plumbing/electrical work is a legal risk.
operational_risks: Skilled craftsmen scarcity; estimating errors; callbacks.
financial_risks: Thin owner margins documented by franchisor P&L.
founder_expertise: Estimating, scheduling, craftsman recruiting; founder not a tradesperson.
staffing: 2-4 W-2 craftsmen + office scheduler by year 2.
automation_potential: Estimating from photos, scheduling, quote follow-up; work manual.
delegation_potential: Moderate — craftsmen and estimators hard to hire.
scalability: Moderate-low — margins thin until multi-territory scale.
expansion: Aging-in-place modifications (grab bars), realtor pre-listing packages, painting (WS18-009).
critical_assumptions: Independent can achieve franchise-level revenue without brand
Royalty add-back flows to profit rather than being consumed by marketing
unanswered_questions: Chicago municipal licensing for handyman scope
failure_modes: Owner discretionary income low single digits (documented in Ace FDD)
score_rationale: Franchise P&L shows median single-territory operators earn ~$40-50k ODI — harsh FCF 3. Access 7, cash 8.
preliminary_verdict: hold — strong demand but FDD P&Ls show thin owner income; viable only at multi-territory scale.

title: Residential painting company (sales-led owner, employed or subcontracted crews)
product_service: Interior and exterior repainting, cabinet refinishing, deck staining; owner sells estimates, production managers run crews.
target_customer: Homeowners in older/affluent suburbs; realtors prepping listings; small landlords.
spending_evidence: MISSING — CertaPro/Five Star Painting Item 19 not retrieved; handyman FDD P&L (similar labor+materials model) shows 43-55% gross profit [B, WS18-S009] as a proxy only.
revenue_mechanism: Fixed-price bids per job (labor + paint).
direct_costs: Crew labor or subcontractor fees, paint/materials, equipment.
working_capital_note: Deposits common (subject to 3-day cancellation right); balance on completion; crews paid weekly.
repeat_purchase: occasional — repaint cycles 5-10 years; referrals key.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed — paint store contractor accounts (Sherwin-Williams, Benjamin Moore dealers).
entry_strategy: Professional sales process, written warranty, fast estimates; founder sells, crews produce.
licenses: Home Repair and Remodeling Act applies (written contract, pamphlet, insurance) [A, WS18-S010, WS18-S011]. EPA lead-safe (RRP) firm certification for pre-1978 homes is required federally (not verified in this run). Municipal licensing MISSING.
operational_risks: Crew quality, weather (exterior season Apr-Oct in Chicago), callbacks.
staffing: Lead painter/production manager early; crews or subs.
delegation_potential: Moderate — production managers available; owner sales initially.
scalability: Moderate — multi-crew operators exist; ceiling limited by crew capacity.
expansion: Cabinet refinishing, epoxy floors, drywall, commercial repaints (WS10).
score_rationale: Fits a sales-willing non-tradesperson owner; low capital; evidence E; crowded.
preliminary_verdict: hold — plausible sales-led model; needs Item 19/margin evidence before advancing.

title: Home inspection firm (licensed, multi-inspector with ancillary tests)
product_service: Pre-purchase home inspections plus radon, sewer scope, mold, termite ancillaries.
target_customer: Homebuyers (referred by buyer agents), sellers (pre-listing).
